findings.reason: two authored, reviewed sections would be left undispatched by the only followup that carries the queueing invocation, exactly the gap that f-qwnw-003 was written to close for 32 and 33.
findings.text: f-qwnw-003 states "Sections 3, 29, 31, 32 and 33 are the plan's remaining implementable work" and invokes `/reckon-build queued-work-needs-no-workaround §3 §29 §31 §32 §33`, while the same document declares s34 and s35 implementable at plan.html:352,356, so a dispatcher following the plan's chain queues neither new section

findings.reason: a worker told to keep consecutive readings inside 180 seconds can satisfy every assertion and leave the observed symptom (a row present while the reading is current) untouched, because the section names no endpoint for a row that outlives the condition that raised it.
findings.text: the Why says the sampler was alive and "the reading it had published was 153 seconds old when read, against a freshness limit of 180 seconds", but the base raises the stale row only when the age exceeds the limit (`published_node_disk_sample`, reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py:748-756), so a 153-second reading cannot have raised a fresh stale row at read time; the figure sits inside the limit the Why gives, so it evidences a row that lingers after the condition clears, not the pass period the rest of the Why blames

findings.reason: one node cannot be closed on one verdict when its gate proves row shape but not freshness, or freshness but not row shape, and the second endpoint is reachable without the first.
findings.text: the Deliverable joins two mechanisms with independent observables: publishing a current reading on a loaded node and across a sampler replacement is one; a stale reading producing a row that names the sampler's process and age and does not hold a session's stop hook is another, and it remains a live case while the first is fixed (a dead sampler publishes nothing at all)

findings.reason: without a base failure for the row assertion, a node can land with that half passing for reasons unrelated to its change and its gate will show nothing.
findings.text: the declared negative control ("with the pass ordered and bounded as measured above, the first assertion fails with a separation above the limit") falsifies only the freshness assertion, so nothing in the section shows the third assertion — the row names the sampler's process and age and is absent from the stop-hook set — failing at the base, where the base's row carries `age_seconds: 0` and an empty `run_id` (reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py:430-441)

findings.reason: the fourth case can be satisfied while the settle-as-promoted endpoint regresses, and the node's single gate then says nothing about which half failed.
findings.text: s34 pairs two mechanisms: a promotion that has completed is recorded as promoted whatever fault follows it, and a failing request stores the module, function and line that raised beside its message; the second is error provenance with its own assertion (the fourth case) and no dependence on the first, so one verdict covers neither
